name: Portico
desc: A see-through arcade of stone arches marching off to a vanishing point — ashlar piers, moulded archivolts and the barrel soffit running back through every opening, with the sun crawling along the run so the lit bay travels; the openings are simply not painted, so whatever is behind reads clean through.

energy.doc: raking-light amplitude, spill through the openings and camera breath

scale.doc: pier height, arcade depth and arch girth (2.2 = colossal; the bay pitch stays fixed so this is never a no-op)

density.doc: how many bays march into depth (3 to 7)

speed.doc: rate the sun crawls along the run; the camera keeps breathing regardless so it never goes static

x.doc: vanishing point across frame — the arcade runs away from here, so this is how you keep the rest of the frame open

side.doc: which way the arcade runs off: to frame right, to frame left, or 'both' to stand inside a double portico

style.doc: aesthetic: warm weathered limestone / Bolognese red terracotta / form from light alone / cyan schematic linework / hatched paper plate

alpha.doc: layer opacity — scales every mark, so it dissolves into the background instead of veiling it
